title: Thoughts on Ego
speaker: Shin-yu Scott Allen
summary: Shin-yu Scott Allen takes up Vasubandhu's Thirty Verses on Consciousness Only, reading the first six verses on store consciousness and manas, the consciousness of self, to look at how ego works. Scott compares karma to a needle wearing a groove in a record, and tells two stories: the Zen master who answers "Is that so?" when accused of fathering a child, and Shin-yu's own anger at drivers merging ahead, who turn out to be Shin-yu's best friend's family. Shin-yu lists bodily signs of ego, such as shallow breathing and muscle tension, and offers tools: counting to ten, slowing the breath, inviting ego in as Thich Nhat Hanh suggests, and consulting mentors. Shin-yu closes by asking the sangha for their own techniques.
